evidence.note: Deliberate runtime probing: lists /app, queries installed runtimes (node/npm/python/sqlite3), checks global npm packages before committing to a stack — genuine environment orientation.

Design is shaped by hard contract constraints from the start: builds a cross-node broadcast hub (broadcast.js) for fan-out and a supervisor that restarts SIGKILLed components within 500ms, directly targeting the node/broadcaster-kill and 60s-recovery resilience rules.

Captures the seq invariant (dedicated seq column, async mutex to serialize) and builds the IRC gateway to write into the same DB/seq stream — reflects internalization of the dense-per-channel-seq-across-protocols rule.
SPA written to 'meet all data-testid requirements' and token storage/localStorage hooks — shows the pinned frontend hook inventory was read and targeted.

Probes the running system against contract specifics: health node_id 0/1/2, cross-node token auth, cross-node write with seq:1 verification, and IRC post continuing the seq — confirms the constraints were understood, not just skimmed.

reasoning: The agent clearly read the contract and captured the main surface plus several hard constraints (dense seq, cross-node fan-out via a broadcaster, kill/recovery resilience, IRC-shares-seq, testid inventory), and it probed the runtime deliberately (versions, ports, foreground start.sh) — well beyond the level-5 anchor. However, the (compressed) trajectory shows no explicit reusable model/checklist of endpoints×status×frames×numerics and no early surfacing of latent contract tensions as an analysis step; internalization is inferred from the design rather than demonstrated through systematic extraction and cross-referencing, so it falls short of the 8/10 anchors. This places it at 6 — between 'captures the main surface' and 'systematically extracts and cross-references the hard constraints.'
